forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Nottinghamshire pension fund identifies 1,700 deceased members still receiving payments
news_drafts.lead: Nottinghamshire's Local Pensions Board has discovered around 1,700 deceased members still recorded as active pensioners, resulting in overpayments the fund is now working to recover. A data cleansing exercise also found approximately 21,000 members with potentially outdated addresses and verified updates for 9,300 others, exposing risks of further payment errors and data breaches. The Administration Monitoring Report attributes part of the growing backlog of unresolved cases to limitations in the fund's Civica pension software, which has been unable to implement system calculations required by recent regulatory changes within required timescales. The board has strengthened governance with the appointment of a new Pensions Manager and an Independent Person to the committee, addressing previously identified resource gaps. The Government's decision to pause local government reorganisation on 7 September has also reduced near-term administrative risk, extending the timeline for capacity challenges the fund had anticipated managing through 2027.

news_drafts.headline: Nottinghamshire forecasts £0.861m overspend for 2026/27
news_drafts.lead: Nottinghamshire's Place Department is forecasting a £0.861m net revenue overspend (day-to-day running costs beyond budget) for 2026/27 even after using planned reserves — money set aside — indicating underlying pressure is larger. The shortfall spans Property Safety and Facilities Management (£0.48m), where higher maintenance and utility costs strain a £0.75m savings target, and Conservation services (£0.28m), reflecting costs of maintaining publicly accessible green spaces. A Baums Lane/A60 highway scheme is running over budget, with the council seeking additional funding from the East Midlands Combined County Authority. Highway repair performance is also under pressure, with 73.2 per cent of defects repaired within 28 days against a 90 per cent target, attributed to historic underinvestment and a severe winter.

findings.headline: Governance improvements: key staff appointments in pension fund
findings.detail: The council has appointed a Pensions Manager and appointed an Independent Person to the Pension Fund Committee and Local Pensions Board. These appointments address previously identified risks relating to vacancies and inadequate resources in pension fund governance.
findings.matters: Filling governance gaps reduces risk of administrative failures and demonstrates management capability in addressing identified staffing weaknesses.

findings.headline: Emerging risk identified: change to pension fund accounting system
findings.detail: The risk register identifies an emerging risk related to changes to the pension fund's accounting system. The paper classifies this as emerging but provides no detail on timing, scope, or potential impact.
findings.matters: Accounting system changes in a pension fund could affect accuracy of fund valuations, compliance reporting, or regulatory returns if not carefully managed.
findings.figures: None - risk listed as emerging with no quantification

findings.headline: New risk identified: contractor may fail to deliver compliant software solutions for pension fund
findings.detail: The risk register identifies a new risk that a contractor may fail to deliver compliant software solutions for the pension fund. No further information is provided on scope, timeline, or likelihood of this risk.
findings.matters: Software delivery failures in pension fund systems could disrupt administration, affect compliance with pensions regulations, or create service failures for scheme members.
findings.figures: None - risk listed as new with no quantification
findings.quote: Adm 9 – Contractor failure to deliver compliant software solutions: New risk

findings.headline: Pension Board adds new risk for payment failures resulting from payroll process change
findings.detail: The risk register adds a new risk for pension payment failures resulting from a change in payroll process. The paper provides no further detail on the scope, timeline, or controls for this change. The full risk assessment is exempt from publication.
findings.matters: Pension payment failure is a critical operational failure that would disrupt benefit payments to pensioners, create legal liability, and damage the council's governance credibility.
findings.quote: Adm 10 – Failures in respect of the payment of pensions caused by a change in payroll process: New risk

findings.headline: Government paused local government reorganisation on 7 September 2026, changing pension fund risk timeline
findings.detail: The council was preparing for local government reorganisation with shadow authority elections planned for 2027. The Government paused this programme on 7 September 2026. This significantly changes the timeline for pension fund administrative capacity risks that were identified as part of LGR preparation.
findings.matters: Pension fund operations would face major disruption during local government reorganisation; the pause removes near-term pressure but creates uncertainty about timing and structure of future changes.
findings.figures: Risk was planned to persist through 2027
findings.quote: Note added regarding the pause placed on the local government reorganisation programme by the Government on 7 September 2026
